body.statement: For each fixed \(n\ge2\), the cylindrical two-plane models in Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:lower\text{-}family\text{-}membership}\) satisfy \(D_H(\theta_0,\theta_h)\asymp_n h^{k+m+1}\) and \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta_0,\theta_h)\asymp_n h^{k+1}\). Only environments targeting coordinates one and two change; integration over the inactive \(\mathbb T^{n-2}\) factor equals one under \(\lambda^{n-2}\), so the active support has two-dimensional volume order \(h^2\) and the powers do not contain \(n\). Constants may depend on the fixed dimension through the family size and mixture normalization. Hence every fixed class containing this family satisfies \(\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\ge c_n\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\) for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\). The two directed aligned losses have the same leading order, so the conclusion holds for the symmetric quotient pseudometric.
body.justification: The lower family certifies the exponent and proves that coordinatewise reparameterizations cannot absorb the leading mixed motion.
body.gap: Liang et al. construct exact plateau rotations; this theorem instead gives a finite-criticality local alternative with explicit nonzero Hellinger and quotient orders.
body.consumer: The result supplies the sharpness benchmark for any recovery algorithm or confidence radius on circular latent variables.
